newsitem.title: ITALY: Autogrill Q1 sales up 2.6 percent.
newsitem.headline: Autogrill Q1 sales up 2.6 percent.

text.p: Italian roadside restaurant chain Autogrill said on Wednesday that its sales in the first quarter of 1997 rose 2.6 percent compared to year ago levels.

The rise was held back by the fall in lottery ticket sales by 30 percent, an area which accounts for 12 percent of group sales. But this was compensated by increased sales of 10.4 percent from the group's bars, restaurants and fast food units in an overall market up 5.4 percent.

This trading update was reported to a shareholders meeting by group chairman Gilberto Benetton and managing director Paolo Prota Giurleo. For the current year, Giurleo said operating results would be in line with those seen in 1996.

The shareholders meeting was called to agree the merger of Autogrill SpA and the listed Finanziaria Autogrill SpA into Edizione's Schemaventidue. Edizione Holding is the private Benetton family company.

After the merger, some 56.50 percent of the group will be owned by Edizione, 13.44 percent by Moevenpick-Holding and 4.85 percent by the San Paolo banking group. The rest of the 25.21 percent will be floated on the stock market.
